changes.before: Before adding anything to cart, measure the body points that affect fit the most. For women, that is usually bust, waist, hip, and dress length. For men, chest, waist, shoulder width, and inseam matter most. For kids, height and weight are often more useful than age alone because matching sets can vary a lot from one cut to another.
changes.after: Start with the size chart for the exact piece you want to order. Check which measurements it asks for and whether it describes body measurements or garment measurements. Follow those instructions and use the same units as the chart. A flat garment width is not the same measurement as a body circumference. If the measurement method is unclear, ask for clarification before choosing a size.

changes.before: Adult women's sizing: fit the most structured area first
changes.after: Adult women's sizing: check the chart for the selected piece

changes.before: For mommy-and-me dresses, tops, and coordinated sets, start with the area that has the least flexibility. If the item is a woven dress, that is usually the bust. If it is a waistband-driven set, that may be the waist or hip. Women should usually buy true to size when the product description shows relaxed silhouettes, stretch fabric, or roomy pajama-style fits. Size up when the piece looks more fitted, when you want extra length, or when you are between measurements and need comfort for all-day wear.
changes.after: For mommy-and-me dresses, tops, and coordinated sets, compare your measurements with the chart for the specific adult piece. Check each listed measurement rather than selecting a size from its letter label or how the outfit looks in a photo. If your measurements fall across different sizes, or the chart does not explain the fit you need, request help before ordering. Do not assume that choosing a larger size will resolve every fit question.

changes.before: For children, age labels are a starting point, not the final decision. A toddler who is tall for age may need the next size up even if the age number sounds right. Older kids and preteens often fit best by height first, then weight, then the garment width if the product page includes it.
changes.after: Measure each child separately using the dimensions requested by the selected product's chart. Use current measurements; an age label alone does not establish fit. Check the available child sizes on that product rather than assuming that every matching style includes the same age range.

changes.before: True to size usually works best for pajamas, softer tees, and easy everyday sets. Sizing up makes more sense for sweaters, seasonal outfits you want to wear for a longer window, or any set you expect to layer. For special-event looks, do not size up too aggressively or the photo-ready shape can get lost.
changes.after: If the outfit will be worn with another layer, or you are planning for a later date, explain that when asking about fit. Avoid automatically ordering a larger size for future growth. The product's measurements and any verified fit instructions should guide the choice.

changes.before: Men's sizing usually comes down to how the shopper likes his tops to fit. If dad prefers a standard tee or shirt fit, true to size is usually the safest move. If he is broad in the shoulders, between sizes, or prefers a looser vacation fit, size up. When in doubt, compare the chest width of a favorite shirt at home to the product page measurements rather than relying only on S, M, L, or XL labels.
changes.after: For daddy-and-me shirts and other adult pieces, check the measurements on the exact product page. A familiar S, M, L, or XL label is not enough to confirm the fit of a different item. If the chart gives garment measurements, you can compare a garment that fits well only when you use the same measurement method. If the chart gives body measurements, follow its body-measuring instructions instead.
What to check for each family member

changes.after: Use the current chart and available options for each selected piece. This checklist is a shopping aid, not a universal size chart or a promise that every style offers the same sizes:

changes.before: Bust, waist, hip S-2XL with garment length notes
changes.after: The measurements requested by the selected adult piece Chart units, measurement method and available size

changes.before: Height, weight, age 2T through teen sizes or age bands
changes.after: Each child's current measurements, as requested by the chart The selected child size rather than age alone

changes.before: Chest, waist, shoulder M-3XL with relaxed or fitted notes
changes.after: The measurements requested by the selected shirt or other piece Whether the chart lists body or garment measurements

changes.before: When to size up versus stay true to size
changes.after: What to do when a size is unclear

changes.before: Stay true to size for cotton tees, soft pajamas, and relaxed matching basics.
changes.after: Recheck the exact product chart, its units and its measurement instructions.

changes.before: Size up when the cut looks fitted, when the fabric has less stretch, or when someone is clearly between sizes.
changes.after: Use verified product details rather than guessing the fit or stretch from a photo.

changes.before: Size up for kids if you want more than one season of wear, but keep event outfits closer to the chart for cleaner photos.
changes.after: Ask for help if measurements fall across sizes or the chart is incomplete.

changes.before: Prioritize comfort over a tighter fit because coordinated outfits only work when everyone is willing to wear them.
changes.after: Check the selected wearer, piece, size and quantity on each cart line before checkout. Matching items may require separate selections; confirm what the product includes.

changes.before: If you are between sizes or ordering for a trip, photo session, or holiday, it is also worth reviewing FAQs before checkout so you have the store's support and policy details in one place.
changes.after: If the product's size chart leaves a question unanswered, contact us before ordering. Include the product name, the selected wearer, and the measurements you need help interpreting.

changes.before: The best final step is to build the cart slowly, checking each family member against the product page rather than treating the whole set as one sizing decision. Start with Matching Outfits, then use FAQs if you need one more confidence check before ordering.
